To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

40% of heterozygous apparent germline TP 53 PVs detected by NGS hereditary pan‐ cancer panel testing are likely to have been acquired somatically, and the majority of these are due to clonal hematopoietic stem cell expansion associated with aging.

approximately 32% of TP53 PV carriers with NGS allele frequency 30%–70% have a somatically acquired variant, and that the clinical utility of TP53 PV detection is limited by the lack of correlation of PV detection with LFS risk.

1) a substantial number of apparent TP53 heterozygous PVs identified by NGS hereditary pan‐ cancer panels are acquired somatically, and 2) the majority of individuals with apparent heterozygosity do not meet classic LFS criteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of germline and somatic variants of the tumor suppressor gene TP53 in a cohort of patients with cancer and their family members.
understanding the origin of TP53 PV detected in hereditary pan‐Cancer panel testing.
improving the quality of hereditary pan‐caner panel testing, which is increasingly used in clinical practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the individual has a pathogenic variant in TP53 and has a germline variant, a somatic variant, or both.
the proband is a TP53 pathogenic variant carrier, but that the variant is not germline in origin, and that it is therefore unclear if they are at elevated risk for Li–Fraumenic cancers.
the proband has a TP53 PV, but that this PV is not germline, and that the proband does not meet criteria for LFS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
1/3 of TP53 variants detected in NGS hereditary cancer panel testing are acquired somatically, and 2/3 of individuals with apparent heterozygote TP53 germline variants do not meet LFS criteria.
approximately 40–45% of apparent TP53 heterozygous variants detected with NGS are likely acquired somatically, and 30% of these variants may be due to constitutional mosaicism.
1 in 5 individuals with an apparent heterozygote TP53 PV are not LFS‐related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of individuals who are found to have an apparently heterozygously germline TP533 PV do not have LFS.
a large proportion of TP53 pathologic variants detected with a hereditary pan‐Cancer NGS panel are likely acquired somatically and not germline in origin.
a substantial proportion of apparent heterozygously inherited TP53 pathogenic mutations are actually acquired somatically.
